title: `Float32` arithmetic stays in `Float32`, and pulls in a double literal
description: Arithmetic on `Float32` is single precision (`3e38 + 3e38` is inf, `16777216 + 1` is 16777216), and `sum` and `mean` of `Float32` are `Float32`. `sum` adds in `Float32` on both engines; the streaming `mean` sums in `f64` and rounds the quotient to `Float32` once (polars-mean-float-streaming). A Python float or int literal takes the column's type, so `Float32 + 0.1` adds 0.1 rounded to a float. Casts between the formats round to nearest (polars-cast-to-double).
The docs are silent on a literal taking a `Float32` column's type: a docs gap.
No upstream test pins single-precision overflow or rounding (`3e38 + 3e38`, `16777216 + 1`); they may change between versions.
reference: `fp32` arithmetic is refused in every profile until #417's stage 3.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

notes: Streaming gives what in memory gives on every probe and observation cited here.
The observations' frames hold a few rows, which streaming runs as one-row morsels; the probes' 6000-row columns cover morsels of many rows.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each probe one row at a time and on a 6000-row column with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')`, and each observation twice: its `df(...)` frame's `select`, `with_columns`, `filter`, `sort`, `unique`, `join` and `group_by` go through the streaming engine the second time (`StreamingFrame`); the `s-` observations collect a lazy query on each engine themselves. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

evidence.note: a dynamic int or float literal takes a float column's type
streaming mean of Float32: f64 sum, quotient cast to f32

provenance.notes: Added to the description: the streaming `mean` of `Float32` sums in `f64` (reduce/mean.rs#L30-L52); the result type stays `Float32`.

evidence.note: literals with a Float32 column stay Float32 (lazy, both engines)
